feature-dev.note: Verified claims hold and covers slide mode, stdin, '' toggle and corrupt-file handling, but the viewer section is prose bullets with fewer concrete signatures and call chains than X.

code-design.note: Per-unit signatures, numbered call chains with explicit error branches, test seams and a numbered assumptions list make every decision pointable; verified line refs, handle_event ordering vs is_help_toggle and the README config-path fix are accurate.

plain.note: Sound core and an extra margin marker, but source:0 default is ambiguous, lazy-flush mis-stamping is left as a risk, and failure paths and signatures are thinner.

superpowers.note: Spec handles code blocks, tables and lazy flush stamping well and has a clear error table, but the 48KB task plan with full code bodies buries decisions and slide mode is simply unsupported.

reason: X separated itself by laying out exact signatures, call chains with a named failure branch at each step, and test seams, so a reviewer can challenge any single unit or decision without wading through code. W was nearly as correct and added useful behaviors but described the viewer wiring less concretely; Z buried its design in a huge code-level plan and Y left the source-line stamping and several failure paths underspecified.
